hook: MotoGP bikes must survive 1.5g braking forces without snapping in two.

sections.voiceover: MotoGP bikes must survive 1.5g braking forces without snapping in two.
sections.visual_cue: Close up of a front brake rotor glowing red under intense heat.
sections.sfx_cue: High-pitched mechanical screech of hard braking.
b_roll: Stock footage of a race bike braking hard on track

sections.voiceover: But how do you keep a bike stable when it is leaning past 60 degrees?
sections.visual_cue: Technical wireframe animation showing the chassis of the RC211V highlighting structural nodes.

sections.voiceover: At these 60 degree lean angles, traditional suspension systems fail to absorb track bumps.
sections.visual_cue: Slow motion shot of a bike chassis flexing mid-corner.
sections.sfx_cue: Low frequency thud of a motorcycle hitting a track bump.
b_roll: Close up of bike frame flexing under load

sections.voiceover: Inside Motorcycles Magazine reports that lateral frame flex acts as a secondary suspension. Australian Motorcycle News confirms this flexibility is vital for rider control.
sections.visual_cue: Split screen showing rigid frame vs flexible frame under lean load.
b_roll: MotoGP racer leaning through a turn

sections.voiceover: Engineers balance vertical rigidity, lateral flex, and torsional stiffness to reach peak performance.
sections.visual_cue: Final shot of the bike exiting a corner at high speed.
b_roll: Race bike accelerating out of a curve
